title_clean: Dhammapada, a Book of Verses, No. 5
description_short: Bhante Bodhidhamma explores the famous Dhammapada verse on how hatred ceases only through love, not through more hatred—an eternal law of non-violence.
description_long:
In this inaugural talk on the Dhammapada verses, Bhante Bodhidhamma examines one of Buddhism's most famous teachings: "Hatred never ceases through hatred in this world; through love alone they cease—this is an eternal law." Drawing from traditional commentary, he shares the story of two rival wives whose bitter feud extends through multiple lifetimes until the Buddha's intervention brings understanding and reconciliation.

The talk explores how we perpetuate cycles of anger and hatred through reactive responses, and offers practical guidance for breaking these destructive patterns. Bhante illustrates this with the story of the Buddha facing Devadatta's wild elephant, demonstrating the abhaya (fearless) posture—standing firm without reactivity while extending goodwill. He emphasizes three key qualities for transforming hostile encounters: fearless stability, compassionate listening to understand the hurt behind anger, and extending goodwill even when friendship isn't possible.

This teaching provides essential guidance for both meditation practitioners and daily life interactions, showing how non-violence and compassionate understanding can heal our hearts and relationships. The discourse demonstrates how ancient Buddhist wisdom offers practical tools for contemporary conflicts and emotional reactivity.
